rows.Incident Description:
At 1655hrs, DM/Mena was notified by Shuttle Bus Team of a traffic collision involving the WP Hotel Shuttle Bus (AB-2821) and a private vehicle (MI-3899). The incident occurred at approximately 1615hrs near the area opposite Crowne Plaza Hotel.  At the time of the incident, there were 25 passengers on board the WP Hotel Shuttle Bus. No injuries were reported.

According to the Shuttle Bus Team, the Hotel Shuttle Bus was en route transferring guests from the Border Gate back to the hotel. While passing through the said area, the shuttle bus attempted to change lanes from the right lane to the left lane and inadvertently collided with the private vehicle (MI‑3899). As a result, the WP Hotel Shuttle Bus sustained minor scratches to the rear left body panel, while the private vehicle sustained minor scratches to the front right bumper and wheel.

The shuttle bus driver immediately reported the incident to the Shuttle Bus Manager and contacted the Traffic Police. Following the incident, nine passengers departed the scene on their own, while the remaining passengers were transferred to a replacement WP Hotel Shuttle Bus (MY‑9241) and conveyed to the hotel without further delay.

Traffic Police were summoned and arrived at the scene to conduct an investigation. Upon review, fault was determined to lie with the WP Hotel Shuttle Bus driver (outsourced vendor GHM). Subsequently, both drivers agreed to resolve the matter privately, and no further dispute was raised. All parties then departed the scene, and WP Hotel Shuttle Bus (AB‑2821) was driven back to the Shuttle Bus Depot for maintenance inspection.

Subsequently, DM proceeded to the East Shuttle Bus Station. Upon arrival, the replacement shuttle bus (MY-9241) had already arrived, and all passengers had been safely dismissed. Confirmation was obtained from the Shuttle/Josephina that no complaints or injuries were reported.

rows.Incident Description:
At 0630hrs, DM/Bill was notified by FOSA/Jackson that Ms. Ji, the registered sharer, had approached the Front Office to raise a complaint regarding the attitude of a Security officer.

According to Ms. Ji, she had proceeded to the South Entrance to wait for her limousine transfer to Zhuhai Airport. Upon arrival, she realized that she had misread the pickup time and that her reserved limousine was scheduled for 0730hrs. As a result, she attempted to wait at the South VIP Reception instead. While at the South Entrance, Ms. Ji was carrying three pieces of luggage and requested assistance from the Security officer stationed there. The Security officer declined to assist. Ms. Ji expressed dissatisfaction with the hotel’s service and stated that both of her arms were scratched as she had to handle the luggage by herself.

DM/Bill assessed Ms. Ji’s condition and observed no open wounds or bleeding, though redness was present on both arms. Medical assistance from the Security Team was offered and declined by the guest. An ice pack was subsequently provided. 

DM/Bill also contacted the Limo Team and successfully arranged for the limousine transfer to proceed immediately. An apology was extended to Ms. Ji for the unpleasant experience, and reassurance was given that a thorough investigation and appropriate training would be conducted with the Security Team. Ms. Ji did not accept the explanation and stated that she would report the incident to her husband, Mr. Wang, the room registrant, and would further pursue the complaint.

Ms. Ji was later escorted to the limousine by DM/Bill and the Bell Team, with luggage assistance provided.

rows.Incident Description:
DM was notified by the Shuttle Bus Team of a traffic collision involving a WM > WP shuttle bus (MX-6624) and a silver van (MR-8169). The incident occurred at approximately 1733hrs at the roundabout along Cotai Strip, near City of Dreams.

At the time of the incident, a total of 45 passengers were on board shuttle bus MX-6624. Traffic Police attended the scene for assessment and investigation.

According to the Shuttle Bus Team and subsequent Traffic Police investigation, the silver van MR-8169 attempted to overtake and changed from the left lane to the right lane without properly observing the surrounding traffic conditions, resulting in a collision with the shuttle bus MX-6624, which was traveling on the right lane.

As a result of the collision, shuttle bus MX-6624 sustained scratches and minor dents on the front left side. The silver van MR-8169 suffered severe damage, including dents to the rear side door and shattered door glass.

One non-inhouse female passenger, Ms. Ho, reported sustaining a twisted injury to her left hand. Following the incident, Ms. Ho and her family (two females and one male) departed the scene with ambulance assistance and were transported to Taipa Kiang Wu Hospital for further medical evaluation. A replacement shuttle bus (MY-9376) was promptly arranged and successfully transferred the remaining 42 passengers from the scene without further delay.
rows.Subject: Traffic Collision - Shuttle Bus
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Investigation:
-After reviewing the shuttle bus CCTV footage,  Traffic Police determined that the van MR-8169 was at fault. The van driver declined to provide further personal information; however,  it was noted that he is a blue card holder,  and his employer attended the scene to provide assistance. -Membership tier of Mr. Guo: N/A

Consolidated investigation with BDV/Anson and CCTV Footage,  timeline as below:
-At 1718hrs,  Mr. Zhou arrived at the North Driveway and parked his Tesla vehicle. He handed the key card holder,  described as a paper‑textured cardholder,  to Valet staff Yang at the Valet Service Counter. After Mr. Zhou exited the vehicle,  both side mirrors and headlights were observed to be turned off.
-At 1719hrs,  Valet staff Yang tapped the key card holder against the vehicle door handle. The vehicle appeared to unlock,  with both side mirrors and headlights turning on. CCTV footage was unable to conclusively confirm whether the key card was dropped at this moment.
-At 1721hrs,  Valet staff Yang parked the vehicle in the basement. At that time,  the headlights were turned off,  while both side mirrors remained turned on.
-At 1740hrs,  Mr. Zhou returned to the North Valet Service Counter and requested retrieval of his vehicle.
-At 1743hrs,  Valet staff Alex arrived at the basement parking area and attempted to retrieve the vehicle. He was able to open the vehicle door by tapping the key card holder; however,  the headlights did not turn on,  while both side mirrors remained turned on.
Subsequently,  it was identified that the Tesla vehicle could not be fully unlocked or operated. At this point,  the Tesla key card was discovered to be missing.
-Following the discovery,  the Valet Team reported the incident to BDV/Anson,  and a check was conducted with the Lost & Found Team. No corresponding Lost & Found record was identified at that time.
-At 1754hrs,  Doorman escorted Mr. Zhou to the basement parking area due to the vehicle being non‑operational.
-At 1757hrs,  Mr. Zhou unlocked the Tesla vehicle using his mobile application,  drove the vehicle,  and departed the property. He requested to be notified should the missing key card be found at a later stage.
-At 2246hrs,  a Doorman found a Tesla car key at the North Entrance driveway,  which matched with the Tesla original stopped area. The car key was handed over to the BDV Captain at 2248hrs.

-During the check-out process at the salon,  the guest did not raise any concerns and completed payment as usual. Subsequently,  while seated with her cousin,  the guest requested GSA Sally to attend to her and informed that her feet felt burned by the paraffin.

-As a service recovery gesture,  the full payment for the service was refunded.

-For more detail,  please refer to Security Log #DL20260112805.

Follow Up:
-Risk Management Team was informed.
-DM please take note.

In response, DM and the Security Team conducted an inspection of Room #571. Upon arrival, the room was found no guest with nor luggage inside. Room #571 has been checked out.

rows.Incident Description:
At 0500hrs, DM/Mena was informed by GSC Team that a male guest call from Room #1140 reported that the room lights had turned on automatically on two occasions despite being switched off via the Crestron System.

DM and the Facility Team attended the room and met with a non‑registered male guest, who declined to provide his personal information and identified himself as a friend of the room registrant, Mr. Hao. During the assessment, the FAC Team inspected the Crestron System and the room control (Slider) panel. Both systems were found to be functioning normally at the time of inspection.

Following a discussion, the guest accepted the recommendation to set the Slider Control Panel to “Lights All Off” and to use the bedside and door‑side Crestron controls to operate the lighting instead. DM further offered to arrange rectification during the room cleaning service on 28Apr26 and extended a fruit platter as a hotel courtesy. The guest accepted the arrangement and did not pursue the matter further at this stage.
rows.Subject: Room Condition - Lights Auto On
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Investigation:
-Membership tier of the registrant Mr. Hao: Diamond Card.
-Unable to obtain information from the non‑registered male guest,  who was advised to be added as a sharer in accordance with hotel policy.

According to the FAC Team:
-The issue was suspected to be caused by a discrepancy between the Slider Control Panel and the Crestron System,  as the bottom of Slider Panel was turning on at that time.

Follow Up:
-Mass ODM was informed.
-DM please take note.
-HSKP Team was informed to coordinate with the FAC & AV Teams to rectify the Slider Control Panel and notified IRD Team for amenities delivery during room cleaning service.

rows.Incident Description:
At 1318hrs, DM/Chris Chan was informed by Housekeeping Team that Mr. Babaroca (65-year-old), the registered guest of Room#515, was standing outside his room requesting ambulance assistance as he was unable to walk.

DM and the Security Team immediately attended the scene and found Mr. Babaroca, who was conscious and seated on a chair provided by the Housekeeping Team. During inquiry, the guest stated that he experienced sudden pain in both knees while walking out of his room, resulting in his inability to walk. He further mentioned a prior injury to his right knee, for which he had previously undergone surgery.

An ambulance was promptly summoned and arrived at the Staff Entrance. Mr. Babaroca was transported to the Staff Entrance via wheelchair by the Security Team and was subsequently transported to CHCSJ for further medical evaluation as per his request. A DM business card was provided to guest and he were advised to contact DM should they require any further assistance. 

As of 1700hrs, the guest remained unreachable. The guest’s host was advised to assist in extending a courtesy call to the guest. The due‑out Room #0515 was checked out following completion of the departure room inspection.
rows.Subject: Ambulance Assistance - Unwell Guest
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Investigation:

-For more detail,  please refer to Security Log #IN20260047352.

rows.Incident Description:
Driver Zhan (Vehicle HK5120) from Chek Chao was assigned to conduct a 12:20 pickup for Mr. Jin Qichang from Encore, with the destination being Hong Kong International Airport. At approximately 12:24, while en route on the Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macau Bridge, Driver Zhan informed Dispatch that the guest requested a change of destination to Zhuhai Airport.

Subsequent verification by the Limousine Team confirmed that the driver had mistakenly picked up the incorrect guest. The passenger was identified as Mr. Yin Guo Dong, whereas the assigned guest was Mr. Jin Qichang.

The Limousine Team immediately informed Mr. Jin Qichang’s host, WM Mass – Qbee Sung, of the situation and arranged a recovery vehicle (Vehicle MY6359) for Mr. Jin. Thus, Mr. Jin was able to board the recovery vehicle with an approximate service delay of 10 minutes.

Mr. Yin Guo Dong’s host, WM Mass – Sue Chan, was also informed accordingly. The Limousine Team attempted to arrange limousine service from Hong Kong International Airport to Zhuhai for Mr. Yin; however, Mr. Yin ultimately opted to reschedule his flight departing from HKIA.
rows.Subject: Staff Error - Chek Chao
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Investigation:
Based on the investigation,  the incident was attributed to Chek Chao Driver Zhan’s failure to adhere to guest verification procedures at pickup. Specifically,  the driver did not properly confirm the guest’s surname and travel destination.

Follow Up:
A formal complaint email has been issued to Chek Chao,  and a request has been made to prohibit Driver Zhan from receiving future assignments.

rows.Incident Description:
At 1612hrs, DM/Chris Chan was informed by the GSC that Ms. Chen, the registered guest of Room #1550, reported that a male stranger had entered her room earlier.

DM immediately attended Room #1550 and met with Ms. Chen inside the room. The guest stated that she checked in at 1238hrs, and the incident occurred at approximately 1608hrs. DM extended a sincere apology for the unpleasant experience and assured the guest that a thorough investigation would be conducted.

Based on the review of Opera and Visionline access records, it was identified that at 1605hrs, Mr. Shen, the registered sharer of Room #1555, approached SFOSA/Lydia at the North Main Registration counter requesting a key reissuance for Room #1555. Due to an operational oversight, two room keys for Room #1550 were mistakenly issued to Mr. Shen instead, which directly led to the unauthorized room entry incident.

Following confirmation of the findings, DM informed Ms. Chen of the investigation results and reiterated apologies for the incident. DM assured the guest that this was an isolated case and advised that appropriate disciplinary action and additional training would be implemented for the concerned team member to prevent recurrence.

As part of service recovery, DM offered an upgrade from two Fountain Suites to two Fountain Parlor Suites, with bellman assistance for luggage handling (Party #5064509, both rooms under Ms. Chen’s name and requested same floor). Additional amenities, including a fruit platter and macarons, were arranged. Furthermore, in view of Ms. Chen’s scheduled departure on 29 April at 1500hrs via Hengqin Port, a departure limousine service and late check‑out until 1500hrs were arranged. Ms. Chen expressed appreciation for the follow‑up and assistance, who did not pursue the matter further.

Separately, at 1616hrs, Mr. Shen approached SFOSA/Lydia again at the Northmain Registration counter regarding the key issuance and reflected the incident. Lydia extended her apologies for the inconvenience caused and offered a fruit platter and a late check‑out until 1400hrs on 29Apr26 as a gesture of goodwill. Mr. Shen accepted the arrangement without further pursuit.
rows.Subject: Guest Complaint - Staff Error
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Investigation:
-Membership tier of the registrant of Room #1550 - Ms. Chen: N/A.
-Membership tier of the registered sharer of Room #1555 - Mr. Shen (WID #83188010): Red Card
-Membership tier of the registrant of Room #1555 - Mr. Zhou (WID #82973920): Gold Card (Mass Marketing)

According to CCTV footage,  Opera and Visionline records:
-At 1603hrs,  Mr. Shen approached SFOSA/Lydia at North Main Registration and presented his ID and membership card.
-SFOSA searched Mr. Shen's membership card and identified Room #1555 in Opera,  then opened guest's ID photo in Opera.
-Subsequently,  she closed the ID photo and the related booking in Opera. She then opened Room #1550 booking in Opera and issued two new room keys.
-No guest identification record associated with Room #1550 was opened or verified during this process.

According to SFOSA/Lydia:
-She mistakenly recalled Mr. Shen’s room number as Room #1550 instead of the correct Room #1555.
-Additionally,  she did not reconfirm the guest’s identification photo prior to issuing the room keys.

-Disciplinary action would be taken against to SFOSA/Lydia.

Follow Up:
-Mass ODM was informed.
-DM please take note and see off guest upon check out.

rows.Incident Description:

DM and the Security Team responded to the scene, where the on-site PSP was handling the situation with both parties. It was learned that the guests had taken a taxi from the North Taxi Station and subsequently had a dispute with the driver regarding the taxi fare.

rows.Incident Description:
At 0024hrs, DM/Chris Lee was informed by GSC that the registered guest of Room #2008, Mr. Ieong, reported finding a hair tie on the TV cabinet that did not belong to him or his girlfriend.

DM and HSKP Team responded to the room immediately and met with the guests. Mr. Ieong stated that he and his girlfriend went out at approximately 1400hrs on 28Apr and discovered the hair tie upon their return to the room at around 0000hrs on 29Apr. He confirmed that no other individual had been invited into the room during their absence.

After reviewing the door lock access record, it was confirmed that only the HSKP Team entered the room at 1524hrs on 28Apr to provide daily make‑up room service, and no other room access was recorded.

DM conveyed the investigation findings to Mr. Ieong and assured him that no unauthorized individual had accessed the room, apart from hotel staff performing daily make-up room service. DM extended apologies for the inconvenience caused, and the hair tie was removed from the room immediately. Mr. Ieong acknowledged the explanation without further pursuit. A fruit platter will be arranged on 29Apr as a gesture of goodwill.
rows.Subject: Guest Concern Regarding Unidentified Item Found in Room
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:

-Membership Tier of the registered guest Mr. Ieong: Gold Card

-At 1323hrs,  guests entered room.
-At 1409hrs,  door opened from inside.
-At 1524hrs,  HSKP entered room.
-At 1540hrs,  door opened from inside. 
-At 0009hrs on 29Apr,  guests returned to the room and report the incident.

-Pending HSKP for further investigation.

rows.Incident Description:
At 1644hrs, DM/Karen was informed by GSC that Mr. Li, the registered guest of Room #1630, had called requesting to speak with the Duty Manager, as his LV T-shirt sent for laundry service was suspected to have experienced color fading during the laundry process.

DM/Karen and the Laundry Team/Timothy attended the room and met with Mr. Li. The Laundry Team explained that all garments are double‑checked prior to processing and presented pre‑laundry photographs, which indicated that color fading was already present on the LV T‑shirt before cleaning.

Mr. Li stated that the T‑shirt had been newly purchased a few days earlier in Macau, worn only once prior to being sent for laundry, and that he did not notice any color fading at the time. After the explanation and review of the supporting photos, Mr. Li accepted the findings and advised that he would contact his LV sales associate directly. He expressed appreciation for the assistance provided and did not pursue the matter further. He was also advised to contact the Duty Manager should any further assistance be required.
rows.Subject: Guest Complaint - Garment Damaged After Laundry Service
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Investigation:
-Membership tier of the registrant - Mr. Li: Diamond Card.

T-Shirt information:
Brand: Louis Vuitton
Color: White
Price: Around MOP 7, 500

According to the Laundry Team/Timothy:
-The Laundry Team had taken photos of the T shirt prior to laundering. Color fading was observed and duly remarked on the laundry form.
-As the guest had signed the agreement section acknowledging and accepting any detected conditions noted on the laundry form,  the Laundry Team proceeded with the cleaning and did not return the T shirt prior to service.

Follow Up:
-Mass ODM was informed.
-DM please take note.

rows.Incident Description:
At 0426hrs, DM/Bill was informed by SFOSA/Kevin that an intoxicated female had approached the North Main Reception, who was unable to respond to any questions during initial engagement.
Security was immediately summoned, and the guest was seated in a wheelchair for safety purposes. A review of CCTV footage confirmed that the intoxicated female had descended from Room #2651. DM subsequently contacted the room, which was answered by a female - later identified as Ms. Wang Haiting (non-registered guest). Ms. Wang identified the intoxicated female as her friend, Ms. Li Zhilin (non-registered guest).

Ms. Wang later arrived at the reception area and, together with the Security team, escorted Ms. Li back to Room #2651 using a wheelchair. Upon arrival, DM and Security conducted a room inspection. Other than vomiting found on the duvet, no additional damage or irregularities were observed.

Ms. Wang stated that both she and Ms. Li were friends of the room registrant - Ms. Yin Ran. DM and Security reiterated the hotel’s registration policy and advised that a cleaning fee might be applied due to the condition of the bedding. Ms. Wang acknowledged and accepted the explanation without further request.

rows.Incident Description:
At 16:32, chauffeur Feng called dispatch office and would need to translation assistant. AM Charlie realized that he was asking for his ferry ticket. Feng drove down to carpark north and another chauffeur Dean passed him the ferry ticket.
Daisy called dispatch office at the same time, Charlie extended apologize and reported that ferry ticket has been passed to FL driver.
rows.Subject: Staff Error - WMP
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Investigation:
14:16 – AM Andy received the ferry ticket and placed it on the whiteboard.
15:55 – Dispatcher Leo dispatched the order to Driver Fang.
16:17 – Driver Fang departed the car park driving vehicle MN6620.
16:18 – Vehicle MN6620 arrived at WPN Casino Entrance.
16:32 – Mr. FL boarded vehicle MN6620 and inquired about the ferry ticket.
16:33 – Driver Fang contacted Dispatch to report the situation,  then proceeded to return to the car park together with Mr. FL in MN6620.
16:35 – Driver Fang met Driver Dean outside the North Valet boom gate,  where Driver Dean was scheduled to deliver the ferry ticket to Mr. FL.
16:35 – Vehicle MN6620 departed the property.
Dispatcher Leo was found to have failed to pass the ferry ticket to the chauffeur after the order was dispatched. ODS record was subsequently updated with a remark indicating that ferry ticket would follow with the pickup. 
The order was originally dispatched to chauffeur Theo,  and after Leo arranged the order to second driver Feng,  he forgot to follow up/update the ferry ticket remark,  which resulted in the incident. Shift managers Herminio,  Andy and supervisor Paul (morning shift),  shift manager Charlie and team leader Rowena (afternoon shift) were not alert the ferry ticket was left behind as well. Shift managers didn't not aware in Teams when the ferry ticket being pickup,  didn't make additional briefing and services standard check during the driver was being arranged.

Follow up:
Reminder: All dispatchers must pay extra attention to all instructions and escalate/alert the shift manager for any top-executive order requirements. Limo management should pay extra attention on high executive orders in order to ensure outstanding service quality,  taking responsibility of the operations.

rows.Incident Item Name: Delay Pick Up or Drop Off - Chek Chao
rows.Incident Description: At 18:53, Host Cicy Tsai informed Chek Chao driver pickup wrong guest for the 18:00 limo booking from WPS to Zhuhai Airport.
rows.Subject: Delay Pick Up or Drop Off - Chek Chao
rows.Investigation/Follow Up 1: Delay Pick Up or Drop Off - Chek Chao
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Investigation:

A cross-border limousine was arranged for Mr. Bai Jipeng from WPS to Zhuhai Airport at 18:00. The Chek Chao coordinator received a report from the driver that a woman,  Ms. Wu,  approached the vehicle at WPS and informed the driver that the booking was made by her friend.

The Chek Chao coordinator then contacted the host,  Cicy Tsai,  to verify the passenger’s identity. Cicy Tsai advised that Ms. Wu should be Mr. Bai’s friend and instructed the driver to proceed.

At 18:53,  Host Cicy Tsai called the Limo Office to advise that Ms. Wu was not the passenger. She declined to settle the charges and arranged another vehicle for Mr. Bai.

rows.Incident Description:
At 1935hrs, DM/Abbie was informed by the Security Control Room that the smoke detector alarm had been activated in Room #2096.

DM, together with the Security and Facilities Teams, promptly attended the room and found Mr. Quan, the registered guest of Room #2096, along with the sharer, Ms. Huang, inside. It was confirmed that there was no fire; however, smoke was present in the room. Further investigation revealed that the alarm was triggered due to the guests smoking cigarettes directly beneath the smoke detector while the air-conditioning was not turned on.

The guests were verbally warned and advised not to smoke under the smoke detector, and to ensure the air-conditioning is turned on should they choose to smoke in the room. The guests acknowledged and understood the hotel’s actions and raised no further concerns.
rows.Subject: Smoke Detector Alarm Activation
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Investigation:
-Membership tier of the registrant - Mr. Quan: Chairman Card.
-Membership tier of the sharer - Ms. Huang: Red Card.

-No announcement nor lift homing during the incident.
-No similar incident happened in the room.
-No injuries,  no damaged item nor complaints during the incident.
-20/F is a smoking floor.

-Please refer to Security Log #DL20260116103 for further details.

Follow up:
-Mass ODM was informed.
-DM please take note.

rows.Incident Description:
At 1903hrs, DM/Karen was informed by the Security Team that a female guest, Ms. Zhang, the registered guest of Room #2325, had earlier been observed taking photographs at Pit #9 inside the casino. The Security Team intervened promptly, instructed the guest to delete the photographs from her mobile phone, and released her after verifying the deletion upon inspection of her device. Ms. Zhang subsequently returned to Room #2325.

Further review of CCTV footage by Surveillance suggested that the guest might have shared the photographs via WeChat. DM and the Security Team then attended Room #2325 and located Ms. Zhang inside the room.

Upon further inspection of Ms. Zhang’s mobile phone and WeChat application, Security confirmed that the photographs taken inside the casino had been deleted and were not shared. Ms. Zhang was verbally warned again by the Security Team. She acknowledged the hotel’s actions and raised no further concerns.
